name: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

predecessors.name: Abbasid Caliphate
predecessors.text: Mosul and Diyar Bakr, the governorship of Hasan Nasir al-Dawla

successors.name: Marwanids of Diyar Bakr
successors.text: the Marwanid share of the former Hamdanid area

successors.name: Fatimid Caliphate
successors.text: Aleppo and northern Syria, under Lu'lu' who 'acknowledged [al-Aziz] as Caliph' in 995

ledger.x: 929: Hasan Nasir al-Dawla governs Mosul and Diyar Bakr, the core of the Hamdanid emirate.
936: Nasir al-Dawla holds the whole Jazira.
942: Nasir al-Dawla rules the caliph's Baghdad as amir al-umara.
943: the Hamdanids leave Baghdad.
944: Sayf al-Dawla takes Aleppo.
944: the Hamdanids and the Ikhshidids fight for northern Syria.
944: Aleppo becomes Sayf al-Dawla's main residence beside Mosul; the page names 'Aleppo (main residence) and Mayyafariqin (Jaziran provinces)' as his capitals.
945: al-Ikhshid recognises the Hamdanids in northern Syria.
945: the October agreement ends the first war for northern Syria; the caliph gave it formal sanction and Sayf married a niece of al-Ikhshid.
946: Sayf al-Dawla takes Damascus after al-Ikhshid's death.
946: the war for Damascus resumes with al-Ikhshid's death in July 946.
947: Damascus stays Ikhshidid.
947: the fight for Damascus ends.
958: the Buyids take Mosul and Nisibis from Nasir al-Dawla.
962: the Byzantines take Anazarbus and Cilicia.
969: the Byzantines take Antioch.
974: the Buyids settle with Abu Taghlib.
978: Adud al-Dawla takes Mosul.
979: the Jazira passes to the Buyids.
979: the Aleppo branch receives Diyar Mudar.
979: Abu Taghlib dies and the fight for the Jazira ends.
989: Hamdanid governors return to Mosul under the Buyids.
990: the Uqaylids end Hamdanid rule at Mosul.
990: the Marwanids take their share.
990: Aleppo is the Hamdanid capital alone.
1002: Lu'lu' takes direct power at Aleppo.
1004: the last Hamdanid rule ends at Aleppo.

wars.name: Hamdanid-Ikhshidid war for Syria
wars.outcome: Sayf al-Dawla took Aleppo (29 October 944), lost Damascus twice and kept northern Syria and the Thughur by the October 945 agreement, with an annual tribute to Egypt; war resumed after al-Ikhshid's death in July 946 and ended in 947 with the 945 terms…

wars.name: Byzantine-Hamdanid wars of Sayf al-Dawla
wars.outcome: Raids and counter-raids on the Cilician and Syrian frontier (Charpete 938, Hadath 948/954/957, Marash 953, Andrassos 960, Raban, Anazarbus 961-962), the sack of Aleppo in December 962, the Byzantine province of Cilicia in 965 and the fall of Antioch in…

wars.name: Buyid-Hamdanid wars over Mosul
wars.outcome: Mu'izz al-Dawla defeated Nasir al-Dawla in January 946, the war was renewed in 948 (tribute and the Buyid names in the Friday prayer), 956-958 (Baghdad briefly taken, Mosul and Nisibis lost in 958) and 964 (Mosul and Nisibis taken again); under Abu Taghlib…

wars.name: Hamdanid campaign against the Fatimids in Syria
wars.outcome: Abu Taghlib, driven from the Jazira, failed to win Damascus from the rebel al-Qassam and was defeated and executed after the battle of Ramla on 29 August 979.

wars.name: Byzantine conquest of Antioch and the Treaty of Safar
wars.outcome: Antioch and the littoral fell in October 969; a treaty of December 969 or January 970 made Aleppo a tributary Byzantine protectorate under Qarquya, with Bakjur as his successor.

wars.name: Bakjur's revolt and the Fatimid attacks on Aleppo
wars.outcome: Bakjur deposed Qarquya in 975; Sa'd retook Aleppo in 977 and Bakjur got Homs; Bakjur attacked Aleppo with Fatimid support in September 983 and Basil II's general Bardas Phokas relieved it; Bakjur was captured and executed after Na'ura in April 991; the…

wars.name: Byzantine-Hamdanid war of 995-1001 (Basil II)
wars.outcome: Basil's forces took Homs, Apamea and Shayzar and besieged Aleppo for eleven months; a peace treaty of 1000 guaranteed Aleppo's survival as a buffer state and a ten-year truce followed in 1001.

wars.name: Uqaylid conquest of Mosul
wars.outcome: The Banu Uqayl occupied Mosul and Diyar Rabi'a in 989 against the Buyids and then turned on the Hamdanid governors, killing Abu Tahir Ibrahim; Uqaylid rule is founded in 990.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey fixes any Hamdanid frontier; the Jazira, the Byzantine marches and the Syrian desert edge are approximate.
